title: QIIME: Moving Pictures of the Human Microbiome
author: Bonnie Hurwitz
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.d5288d
materials: Make sure the QIIME software is loaded on the hpc. module load qiime

steps.title: Download tutorial dataset
steps.instruction: Retrieve the Moving Pictures tutorial archive with wget or curl: `wget ftp://ftp.microbio.me/qiime/tutorial_files/moving_pictures_tutorial-1.9.0.tgz` or `curl -O ftp://ftp.microbio.me/qiime/tutorial_files/moving_pictures_tutorial-1.9.0.tgz`.

steps.title: Enter analysis directory
steps.instruction: Change to the Illumina data directory: `cd moving_pictures_tutorial-1.9.0/illumina`.

steps.title: Validate mapping file
steps.instruction: Run QIIME’s mapping‑file validator to ensure `map.tsv` is correctly formatted: `validate_mapping_file.py -o vmf-map/ -m map.tsv`. If errors are reported, edit the file and rerun the command.

steps.title: Demultiplex and quality filter reads
steps.instruction: Assign barcodes and filter low‑quality reads (files may remain gzipped) with: `split_libraries_fastq.py -o slout/ -i forward_reads.fastq.gz -b barcodes.fastq.gz -m map.tsv`.

steps.title: Count retained sequences
steps.instruction: Report the number of sequences after demultiplexing: `count_seqs.py -i slout/seqs.fna`.

steps.title: Perform open‑reference OTU picking
steps.instruction: Cluster sequences into OTUs using the open‑reference method: `pick_open_reference_otus.py -o otus/ -i slout/seqs.fna -p ../uc_fast_params.txt`. The parameters file enables reverse‑strand matching. Primary outputs are `otus/otu_table_mc2_w_tax_no_pynast_failures.biom` (OTU table) and `otus/rep_set.tre` (phylogenetic tree).

steps.title: Configure matplotlib backend
steps.instruction: Create the file `~/.config/matplotlib/matplotlibrc` and add the line `backend : agg` so QIIME can generate non‑interactive plots.

steps.title: Run core diversity analyses
steps.instruction: Execute the main diversity pipeline (using a sampling depth of 1114): `core_diversity_analyses.py -o cdout/ -i otus/otu_table_mc2_w_tax_no_pynast_failures.biom -m map.tsv -t otus/rep_set.tre -e 1114 -c SampleType,DaysSinceExperimentStart`.

steps.title: Rerun diversity with recovery
steps.instruction: If the previous run failed or you need additional categories, rerun with recovery: `core_diversity_analyses.py -o cdout/ --recover_from_failure -c SampleType,DaysSinceExperimentStart` (use the same input files as before).

steps.title: Create custom mapping file
steps.instruction: Manually compose a tab‑delimited mapping file containing at least the columns `SampleID`, `BarcodeSequence`, `LinkerPrimerSequence`, `Treatment`, `DOB`, and `Description`. Leave `BarcodeSequence` and `LinkerPrimerSequence` empty if they are not needed.

steps.title: Validate custom mapping file
steps.instruction: Check the newly created mapping file with: `validate_mapping_file.py -m -o check_id_output/ -p -b` (adjust options as needed for your file).

steps.title: Convert fasta to QIIME format
steps.instruction: For each demultiplexed sample, run the provided Perl script to prepend the sample ID to each sequence header and append the result to `slout/seqs.fna`.

substeps.instruction: for sample in `cat samples`; do ./convert_to_qiime.pl $sample.fna $sample; done

description: To compute some summary statistics of the OTU table we can run the following command. The key piece of information you need to pull from this output is the depth of sequencing that should be used in diversity analyses. Many of the analyses that follow require that there are an equal number of sequences in each sample, so you need to review the Counts/sample detail and decide what depth you'd like. Any samples that don't have at least that many sequences will not be included in the analyses, so this is always a trade-off between the number of sequences you throw away and the number of samples you throw away. For some perspective on this, see Kuczynski 2010 . biom summarize-table -i otus/otu_table_mc2_w_tax_no_pynast_failures.biom
